reason: Pre-implementation independent review proved two R2 defects while the backend module branch was still clean: NORMAL high-risk publish/apply authority is represented by a sealed STEP_UP_REQUIRED eligibility package rather than ALLOWED, and the dedicated People credential must be body-confined so it cannot become a general product-authority oracle. No R2 backend source or test had been edited or run when this correction was raised.

provenPreImplementationState.rule: R3 corrects authority before implementation; it does not invalidate or repeat an implemented or tested delta.

supersession: R2 originEvidenceRecalculation.authDecision ALLOWED-only text is replaced by decisionByRiskAndMode below.
R2 exactTouchBoundary is extended only by ProductSurfaceAuthorityController.java and ProductSurfaceAuthorityControllerTest.java.
R2 dedicatedCredentialContract is strengthened by the authenticated-caller requestBodyGuard below.
R2 Auth A1 adds one exact controller guard test class; R2 People P1 remains unchanged.
Every other R1 and R2 restriction, exact seven-tuple registry, hash rule, default-OFF rule and no-merge/no-activation rule remains binding.

mediumTuples.rule: Require exactly one sealed capability grant, exactly one selected source scope, exact routeGrantRef, exact readOnly=false and complete revisions. revalidateAt is mandatory and future; result, scope and grant validUntil values are nullable but must be future when present, and effective freshness is the earliest value that exists. STEP_UP_REQUIRED or any other decision denies.

normalMode.requiredAssurance: Must exactly equal the nonblank dwp.hris.experience.origin-authority.required-assurance setting.

highRiskTuples.sharedRule: Require exactly one sealed capability grant, exactly one selected source scope, exact routeGrantRef, exact method/readOnly and complete revisions. revalidateAt is mandatory and future; result, scope and grant validUntil values are nullable but must be future when present, and effective freshness is the earliest value that exists. The STEP_UP_REQUIRED observation is receipt-read evidence of current eligibility only; it must never be relabeled ALLOWED, reused as a mutation permit or accepted for a medium tuple.

decisionByRiskAndMode.accessModeRule: Evaluate exactly once with the current HcmPepContext.activeAccessMode. NORMAL and ELEVATED are the only accepted modes; no retry, fallback, mode substitution or PROVIDER_SUPPORT is allowed.
decisionByRiskAndMode.historicModeBinding: The existing Gateway creates ordinary high-risk command authority in NORMAL mode, forwards the exact STEP_UP_REQUIRED decision/context/scope to People, and People verifies the signed step-up challenge separately without converting HcmPepContext to ELEVATED. The V54 publish/apply receipt therefore stores the NORMAL decision and context evidence. Do not synthesize ELEVATED historical evidence or re-evaluate a second mode.
decisionByRiskAndMode.revisionRule: For either accepted high-risk form, reproduce the Gateway product evaluation revision from the exact returned Auth revisions, current mode, route and routeGrantRef, then apply the existing family-specific V54 authorization/context algorithms from R2. Stored values remain comparison-only.

requiredAssuranceConfiguration.rule: Feature default remains OFF. When enabled, a blank setting makes high-risk origin proof unavailable and therefore opaque 404; it never weakens comparison.

requestBodyGuard.authenticatedCallerSource: ProductSurfaceInternalSecurityConfig must place its successfully authenticated exact service identity in a request attribute. ProductSurfaceAuthorityController may apply the People guard only from that trusted attribute, never from an unverified body or raw caller assertion.

allowedBody.contextScopeKey: An exact ProductSurfaceScopeKey.key(tenantId, actorId, 'hcm', 'hcm.operations', source, kind) value from routeAllowedSelectors; arbitrary nonblank or merely well-formed values are denied before authority evaluation.

requestBodyGuard.selectorConstructionRule: The controller recomputes every candidate from the validated body tenantId and actorId plus the fixed product, surface, source and kind. It accepts an exact equality with one route candidate only; a selector for another tenant, actor, route profile, product or surface is denied.
deny: Any other product, surface, access mode, route, supplied context key, blank, non-trim-stable, merely well-formed or recomputation-mismatched scope selector, support field or support scope.
Any request that bypasses the authenticated People caller attribute or mixes dedicated People and existing credential headers.
Any People request whose returned route, capability, scope, routeGrantRef or freshness does not close exactly against the independent R2 registry.
requestBodyGuard.existingCallerRule: Gateway, Platform and Meeting behavior and bodies remain unchanged; only the authenticated dwp-people-server branch receives this additional body guard.

stillForbidden: all other files outside the combined exact R2 plus R3 boundaries
Gateway, generated contract, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, frontend application and Notification edits
runtime activation and merge to dwp-dev

targetedVerification.peopleP1: Use the exact unchanged R2 People P1 command; no wildcard, migration, Postgres, frontend or repository-wide test is authorized.
targetedVerification.policy: Run A1 and P1 once only after the combined static implementation is complete. After a failure rerun only the smallest owning class, then one final aggregate for the changed cluster only if the fix crosses that cluster.

completionGate: High-risk NORMAL and ELEVATED positive cases close under their exact sealed decision and activation state, while medium STEP_UP and every cross-mode substitution deny opaquely.

The dedicated People credential cannot evaluate any non-HCM product/surface, non-origin route, provider-support request, supplied context, missing or arbitrary selector, another tenant/actor selector or support-bearing request.
Wrong caller attribute and all cross-token, mixed-header, wrong-path and wrong-method cases deny without changing Gateway, Platform or Meeting behavior.
The exact A1 and P1 clusters pass, changed paths equal the combined R2/R3 allowlist, V56 and accepted frontend bytes remain unchanged, and independent review reports P0=0/P1=0.
